lines: +# OE-STEP optimization notes
+## Result summary (bench, dev set, warmup + 1 timed step unless noted)
+| config | step (s) | rollout (s) | train+sync (s) | speedup vs ref |
+| E1: ref-skip + selective recompute + spec 4/5 | 739.4 | 509.7 | 229.7 | 0.999 |
+| E2: E1 − spec change + MoE config + routed-experts delta | 681.1 | 430.9 | 250.2 | 1.084 |
+| E3: E2 + JIT router topk + 49152 tok/microbatch | 604.8 | 387.8 | 216.9 | 1.221 |
+| E4b (FINAL): E3 + grad-buffer no-CPU-backup | 596.9 | 388.7 | 208.1 | 1.237 |
+All of E1/E2/E3/E4b passed every bench gate (identity, staleness, weights
+cos ≈ 0.79 ≥ 0.675, logprob within caps). Final config was additionally
+validated with `bench --steps 2` (verifier protocol: warmup + 2 timed steps).
+Baseline phase split (from miles timers, warmup step): rollout 459s,
+log_probs (actor fwd) 40s, ref_log_probs 51s, actor_train 227s,
+sleep ~6-31s, update_weights ~7s.
+## What was changed (final configuration)
+Launch (`/app/launch/run_step.py`), vs baseline:
+- `--recompute-granularity selective --recompute-modules moe_act mla_up_proj`
+  (was full recompute). Peak train memory still fits easily; actor_train
+  227s → ~190s (warmup) at same microbatch size.
+- `--max-tokens-per-gpu 49152` (was 32768; 63 → 39 microbatches).
+  actor_train −16% and log_probs −25% (timed step). Dynamic-batch partitions
+  stay token-balanced, so the per-microbatch MTP loss normalization is
+  effectively unchanged (router-gate cosine unchanged ~0.79).
+- Env `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_KERNEL_GROUPED_TOPK=1` for the engines.
+Miles (`/root/miles`):
+1. `backends/megatron_utils/actor.py` — skip the reference-model forward pass
+   when both KL coefficients are zero (`--kl-coef 0` and `--kl-loss-coef 0`,
+   which is the locked config). The ref log-probs cannot influence advantages,
+   loss or gradients in that case; the actor's own log-probs are aliased into
+   `ref_log_probs` so downstream code/metrics keep working (KL metric reads
+   exactly 0). Saves the full 51s ref forward + weight swap per step.
+2. `backends/megatron_utils/lora/utils.py` + `model.py` — in colocate mode,
+   allocate DDP *grad* buffers without a torch-memory-saver CPU backup
+   (`disable_grad_buffers_cpu_backup`). Gradients are dead while the trainer
+   is paused (consumed by the optimizer step, zeroed before next backward);
+   param buffers keep their backup. Sleep after train 28s → 24s.
+3. `rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py` — client side of the
+   routed-experts delta protocol (below): reassembles the full-sequence
+   routing array from per-turn deltas.
+SGLang (`/sgl-workspace/sglang/python`):
+1. `srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py` —
+   routed-experts **delta protocol**. Baseline: every turn response carries
+   routing for the *entire* context (avg ~13k rows × 47 layers × 4 experts ×
+   int32, base64; ~32 GB per step across engines). Now a conversation that
+   passes `custom_params{oe_ep, oe_turn}` receives only rows not yet sent,
+   prefixed with one header row (magic, fmt, start, conv-key hash, turn,
+   rows, layers, topk); expert ids are packed 4-per-int32 when they fit in
+   uint8 (checked per payload, int32 fallback otherwise). Any other caller
+   gets the legacy full payload. Client merge was validated **bit-exact**
+   against legacy payloads for full episodes. Harness: 745 → 787 tok/s
+   (+5.6% at 25 turns; more at full length).
+2. `srt/layers/moe/topk.py` — admit the fused JIT router gate for
+   single-group routing (`num_expert_group >= 1` on CUDA; previously `> 1`,
+   which excluded GLM-4.7-Flash's n_group=1 and fell back to a chain of
+   torch ops incl. `torch.topk`). Unit-verified bit-exact ids and fp32-exact
+   weights vs the reference impl for GLM's exact router params (sigmoid+bias,
+   topk 5 incl. fused shared, renormalize, scaling 1.8). Harness: 787 →
+3. Tuned fused-MoE Triton configs for this model's exact shapes, which
+   SGLang lacked (it logged "Using default MoE kernel config"):
+   `.../moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_7_1/E=65,N=1536,device_name=NVIDIA_H200{,_down}.json`,
+   generated with a focused sweep over M ∈ {8..8192}. Profiled
+   `fused_moe_kernel` time −10%.
+4. `srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py` — session-affinity DP routing
+   (pin a conversation id to one DP rank). **Inert in the final config**
+   (dp_size=1); kept from the DP-attention experiment below.
+## How rollout time was diagnosed
+Standalone harness (bare SGLang + oracle plugin + replay client) for fast
+A/Bs, plus torch-profiler traces of a live engine: `fused_moe_kernel` ~56%
+of kernel time (weight-bandwidth-bound at tiny token counts, ~3.4 TB/s eff.),
+FlashAttention MLA ~12%, router topk (torch fallback) ~5%, routed-experts
+readback ~5% more. Decode throughput per GPU was flat across TP1/TP2/TP4
+(~700-745 tok/s), ruling out simple TP scaling: bigger batches just touch
+more experts per forward.
+## Ideas tried that did not work
+- Speculative decoding beyond baseline (steps/draft 2/3): deeper chains
+  (3/4, 4/5) and trees (topk 2-4) all *slower* end-to-end (accept len
+  2.06→2.49 but draft MTP forwards over long KV cost more than they save).
+  No-spec: 541 tok/s. Baseline 2/3 is optimal here.
+- Engine topology: TP2 (704 tok/s/GPU), TP4 (~700/GPU) — flat vs TP1 (745).
+  DP-attention+EP4 with standard dispatcher: 580/GPU (DP lockstep imbalance
+  + dispatch overhead at small batches). DeepEP: bf16 requires low-latency
+  mode, which caps dispatch tokens and breaks prefill. All abandoned;
+  4×TP1 kept.
+- `--disable-chunked-prefix-cache` (absorbed-MLA extend): 745→745, no-op.
+- flashinfer / flashmla attention backends: 712 / 707 vs fa3 745.
+- DeepGEMM MoE runner: 459 tok/s (much worse at these batch sizes).
+- FP8 rollout quantization: `--quantize-and-serve` needs ModelOpt; not
+  pursued further (log-prob gate risk + weight-sync integration unknowns).
+- `--max-tokens-per-gpu 65536`: OOM in train (133 GiB) with selective
+  recompute; 49152 is the safe point.
+- `--no-offload-train` (+ mem-fraction re-tune): eliminates the 24s sleep +
+  7s wake in principle, but the trainer's training-peak reserved memory then
+  blocks engine weight/KV resume (torch-memory-saver OOM on wake). Would
+  need trainer cache clearing + tighter KV budget; judged too risky for ~5%.
+- `--skip-actor-forward-only`: would save the 35-46s actor log-prob forward
+  (π_old ≡ current policy for one step/rollout), but is incompatible with
+  the required `--save-debug-train-data` dump (trainer `log_probs` would be
+  missing), which the log-prob gate needs. Not used.
+- MTP fused linear cross-entropy: MTP logits traffic ≈ 2 TB/step ≈ 0.6s;
+  fused CE recomputes logits in backward — no win. Not used.
+## Semantics safety
+- Model/data/order/group/batch, LR/optimizer, loss normalization, sampling:
+  untouched. `--use-rollout-routing-replay` stays on; routing arrays are
+  bit-identical to baseline (validated). Router topk replacement is
+  bit-exact. The ref-forward skip is exact when both KL coefficients are 0.
+  Selective recompute and microbatch size change only kernel scheduling /
+  accumulation order. Staleness: weight sync flow unchanged; bench shows
+  one weight version per step, distinct across steps, in every run.
